pull_request.title: Infrastructure: Add reusable literature reading tools and ATLAS/CMS source maps
pull_request.head: m0/reference-reading-pilot
pull_request.body:
## Summary

The reference collection had download checksums but no reusable page text or
navigation maps. Add a pinned local PDF reader with extraction, literal search,
selected rendering and hash-verified cache reuse, plus guides for five documents:
ATLAS Pixel TDR, CMS Tracker TDR, RD53A manual, and the ATLAS/CMS JINST overviews
(1,712 pages in total).

The guides record source versions, physical/printed page mappings, reading
coverage and caveats, including RD53A's stale contents and the distinction between
TDR requirements, prototype hardware and simulation assumptions. Whole-detector
maps and a literature-coverage assessment frame realistic component use for
simulation. Source metadata, overview acquisition receipts and curated session
records preserve provenance; PDFs, full text, renders and environments stay ignored.

## Scope and governance

- M0 infrastructure and literature work, on `m0/reference-reading-pilot`.
- ADR-005 remains DRAFT; related logging workflow: ADR-004.
- Direct user requests; no linked issue.
- No detector geometry, material, reconstruction configuration or sign-off changes.
- DD4hep/XML generation remains a future discussion.

## Validation

- 7 synthetic reader tests, 15 logging/document-link tests and 4 downloader tests.
- 12 known-answer retrieval checks across the five local documents, with
  contiguous page coverage and the original RD53A footer checks.
- Source/cache hash verification and selected rendered-page inspections.
- Session-record validation and `git diff --check`.

Exact results, source/tool versions, hashes and measured timings are retained in:

- [Original pilot](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/m0/reference-reading-pilot/docs/validation/reference-reading-pilot.md) and paired JSON.
- [CMS Tracker extension](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/m0/reference-reading-pilot/docs/validation/cms-tracker-reading.md) and paired JSON.
- [Overview intake](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/m0/reference-reading-pilot/docs/validation/overview-reading.md) and paired JSON.

These are extraction and sampled-reading checks, not a complete scientific review.
No OCR, validated table transcription or public/local PDF byte comparison is
claimed. PyMuPDF licensing is recorded in the catalogue. Review cache provenance,
page navigation and reading limits before the next focused evidence pass.

events.text:
Yes—the two inputs are **ATLAS and CMS integration of RD53 into their detector designs**. The chip manual supports that comparison.

**We have enough resources locally to begin every subsystem, but not yet enough verified evidence to promise the same construction-level detail throughout.**

### Already available

I checked the local PDF titles:

| System | ATLAS resources | CMS resources |
|---|---|---|
| Pixels | Pixel TDR; RD53C-ATLAS manual | Tracker TDR; RD53C-CMS manual |
| Strips / outer tracker | Strip TDR **025** | Tracker TDR **014** |
| Calorimeters | LAr upgrade **027**; Tile upgrade **028** | Barrel upgrade **015**; endcap upgrade **019** |
| Muons | Muon upgrade **026** | Muon upgrade **016** |

The shared RD53A manual is also available. Most of these documents still need the extraction and reading pass we performed for pixels.

### What is missing

The main gap is **upgrade documentation versus complete detector construction**. We should supplement the upgrade TDRs with:

- **Original/as-built construction references:** absorbers, active layers, cryostats, chamber stacks and supports. Original calorimeter reports are listed separately in the [ATLAS TDR index]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).
- **Component and integration documentation:** hybrids, readout assemblies, adhesives, cooling, cables and interfaces.
- **Later production and qualification results:** to distinguish TDR proposals from what was built and tested.
- **Material and validation evidence:** compositions, masses, service routing and measurements sufficient to check our simulation.

For comparable detail, each subsystem needs the same chain: **active element → readout → assembly → support/services → validation**.

### Suggested next step

Start with **ATLAS strips and CMS Outer Tracker**, using the existing PDFs. Then map calorimeters and muons and produce a precise missing-document list for each. **No additional downloads are needed to start.**

Saved this assessment in [literature-coverage.md]([redacted] and logged it. Fifteen documentation/logging tests and validation of eight session records passed. ADR-005 remains draft; no detector changes were made.

events.text:
Would the actual TDRs of ALTAS and CMS help to get the overall picture ? 

Just to set the scene correct:
- we do not aim for CAD/engineering like accuracy in this project, we want to make the usage of the components in the detector realistic
- and then we want to auto-generate DD4hep factory and xml code to build this detector in good accuracy with Geant4 (we will discuss this later)
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text: That clarifies the target: realistic component use and detector integration, at the level needed for simulation. I’ll record that distinction and check which whole-detector references best complement the subsystem TDRs.
events.content_kind: visible_message; conservative redactions recorded in source

events.text:
**Yes—whole-detector references would help establish the overall picture:** how subsystems fit together, where components sit, and how magnets, supports and services constrain their use.

For that purpose, I recommend adding these comprehensive detector-description papers alongside the TDRs:

- [The ATLAS Experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider]([external URL redacted; see source journal])
- [The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC](https://cds.cern.ch/record/1129810/)

These describe the original detectors; the upgrade TDRs supply the subsequent changes.

### Your clarification changes the emphasis

My previous resource list put too much emphasis on construction detail. **Our target is simulation-relevant realism.** We need credible:

- component dimensions, placement, repetition and segmentation;
- active and passive materials;
- supports, cooling and services where they affect material or integration;
- sensitive regions and readout mapping.

Small details can use documented effective representations—for example, a service bundle represented by its envelope and material composition, without modelling every wire. Conversely, thin layers may deserve explicit treatment when their material contribution matters.

### The intended destination

I understand the workflow as:

**Literature → reviewed detector/component specification → generated DD4hep factories and XML → Geant4 validation.**

The literature pass should therefore capture physical structure, parameters, provenance and justified approximations in a form that can later support generation. We can discuss the generator architecture and quantitative accuracy targets separately, as you suggest.

I recorded this clarification in the repository’s [coverage assessment]([redacted] Session validation passed; no implementation or design approval was introduced.
